incidents.victim: US-based relatives of Taiwanese government official
incidents.vector: California woman acting as an unregistered PRC agent conducted physical surveillance on US-based targets over a three-month period, directed and tasked by PRC government officials.
incidents.impact: PRC-directed covert surveillance of a Taiwanese official’s relatives on US soil exposed; suspect arrested at LAX on October 5, 2026 before boarding a flight to China. Charges include acting as an unregistered foreign agent.

incidents.victim: US AI policy experts (think tanks, universities, law firms)
incidents.vector: China-linked actors impersonated former US government officials including White House OSTP staff and economists, building trust before delivering adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) phishing links to fake Microsoft and OneDrive portals that bypass MFA.
incidents.impact: Cloud account credentials stolen from AI policy researchers at leading US institutions; operation supports Chinese intelligence objectives to monitor US AI regulatory planning and policy positions. Campaign active since at least April 2025.

incidents.vector: DataSuckers extortion group exfiltrated data from company servers, then posted a ransom demand directly on ATB’s website demanding $400,000.
incidents.impact: Attackers claim 7.9 million customer records stolen including names, phone numbers, emails, addresses, and password hashes, plus employee passport data and 11 million order records. ATB disputes the breach; investigation ongoing.

incidents.vector: Attacker exploited a domestic company’s legitimate API access to the Central Person Register (CPR) to conduct automated mass enumeration of records during September 2026.
incidents.impact: Names, home addresses, and CPR numbers (national identity numbers used for healthcare, banking, and all government services) for approximately 8.8 million people — essentially the entire Danish population — exposed. CPR numbers cannot be changed, creating permanent identity-fraud risk.

incidents.vector: Attackers breached servers operated by an outside vendor used by Daiwa Securities to process customer data.
incidents.impact: Personal information for up to 110,000 Daiwa customers potentially stolen; Daiwa’s own systems were not compromised. Data alone cannot be used to access accounts or execute trades.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to servers hosting the MrMax app and online store; method of initial access not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: Personal data for up to 1,735,154 members potentially leaked including member IDs, names, email addresses, and phone numbers. No credit card or password data affected. Services temporarily suspended while investigation proceeds.

incidents.victim: ATNS — Air Traffic and Navigation Services (South Africa)
incidents.vector: Ransomware-linked malware was introduced into the OT network that provides real-time weather data for air traffic controllers; employee collusion is suspected as the access vector.
incidents.impact: OT systems providing meteorological services for air traffic management were compromised; ATNS manages approximately 6% of the world’s airspace and the attack could have disrupted international flight operations. Attack was contained; no flights were cancelled.

incidents.vector: Separate intrusions: a Microsoft 365 employee account was compromised and used to send approximately 9,000 phishing emails to journalistic sources; a Google Workspace account was accessed unauthorized from July 2026 onward.
incidents.impact: Approximately 1,646 individuals’ data potentially exposed via the Google Workspace breach; journalistic sources targeted by phishing from a trusted Nikkei domain. Both accounts have been secured.

incidents.victim: Government and national security organizations across Asia
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing with cloned Gmail attachment interfaces delivered a five-stage infection chain culminating in the “Antino” Rust backdoor; command-and-control traffic routed through Microsoft 365 OneDrive to blend with legitimate traffic.
incidents.impact: Approximately 350 endpoints compromised across 8 countries (Taiwan, India, Philippines, Cambodia, Pakistan, Thailand, Myanmar, Syria), spanning defense, military, foreign affairs, legislative, and civil society organizations. Long-running intelligence collection campaign assessed as active from September 2025 through at least July 2026.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters exploited an Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day (CVE-2026-35273) using URL-encoding to bypass WAF mitigations; the same technique was simultaneously used against dozens of organizations across higher education, technology, healthcare, and government.
incidents.impact: Social Security numbers, psychiatric evaluation files, and details of clandestine work assignments for more than 5,000 FBI officials stolen and publicly exposed. One Dutch ShinyHunters member arrested in September; Accenture contractor removed from FBI. Breach disclosure confirmed.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised one of three hot wallet layers maintained by the platform; specific access method not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: More than $350 million in cryptocurrency stolen from customer funds, making it the largest crypto heist of 2026. Funds were quickly dispersed across multiple chains.

incidents.victim: University of Illinois Chicago — College of Medicine
incidents.vector: Booba ransomware (assessed as a rebrand of Frag ransomware) deployed on College of Medicine systems; initial access vector not disclosed.
incidents.impact: 344 GB of data claimed stolen, including patient and research data from a top US medical school. Hospital systems have been restored; investigation ongoing.

incidents.victim: Global organizations using Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway
incidents.attacker: Unknown — multiple actors including state-suspected groups
incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of two unauthenticated RCE zero-days in Citrix NetScaler (CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, CVSS 9.5 each) for at least three weeks before public disclosure; a third vulnerability (CVE-2026-88779, CVSS 8.7 DoS) was disclosed Oct 5 and can chain with the RCE pair. Over 50,000 vulnerable instances identified globally.
incidents.impact: Confirmed breaches of government, financial services, technology, education, and legal organizations across North America and Europe; advanced and state-suspected threat groups observed among attackers per Mandiant. CISA, NCSC, and Unit 42 all issued active-exploitation warnings. Patching urgently required.

incidents.vector: A misconfigured file-sharing server at the Defense Manpower Data Center was left accessible to unauthorized users for approximately nine months.
incidents.impact: Names, military information, and Social Security numbers of approximately 2.8 million living and 294,000 deceased US military personnel exposed over a nine-month window (October 2025 – July 2026). Affected individuals are being notified.

incidents.victim: Medyc and MyDr (Polish healthcare software platforms)
incidents.vector: Hacking of cloud-hosted healthcare software platforms used by clinics and medical providers across Poland; same criminal group responsible for both breaches.
incidents.impact: Medyc: 5 million patient records stolen; MyDr: 19 million records stolen — combined exposure of approximately 24 million patient records including diagnoses, prescriptions, and personal identifiers.

incidents.attacker: China — state-suspected espionage groups (two distinct groups)
incidents.vector: Two China-nexus threat groups have exploited a pre-authentication RCE vulnerability in the TACACS+ network authentication protocol over the past two years, enabling persistent access to core routing and switching infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Persistent footholds and lateral movement achieved in telecom networks across multiple countries; TACACS+ governs authentication on virtually all enterprise network equipment. Scope of data collection is not yet publicly confirmed.

incidents.vector: Active-duty US Army soldier with a secret-level security clearance exploited exposed Snowflake cloud storage credentials to download bulk call and text metadata from AT&T and other telecom providers.
incidents.impact: Call and text metadata for more than 100 million AT&T customers stolen; AT&T paid a $370,000 Bitcoin ransom. Soldier Cameron Wagenius sentenced September 25, 2026 to 70 months in federal prison; co-conspirators still face charges.

incidents.victim: Fideuram (private banking arm of Intesa Sanpaolo, Italy)
incidents.vector: Fraudsters used AI-generated audio to convincingly impersonate the CEO of Intesa Sanpaolo and persuaded Fideuram executives to authorize wire transfers to accounts in China and Hong Kong.
incidents.impact: €95 million ($108 million) stolen in February 2026; approximately €59 million subsequently recovered but €36 million remains missing. Represents one of the largest confirmed AI-assisted fraud cases to date.
